exposure: Anxiety level (measured by Beck Anxiety Inventory - BAI scores)
Choice of anesthesia method (general anesthesia vs. spinal anesthesia)
cohort: The study included 150 pregnant women: 100 scheduled for elective caesarean section (50 preferring spinal anesthesia, 50 preferring general anesthesia) and 50 undergoing normal spontaneous vaginal delivery (control group).
finding: Pregnant women with higher anxiety levels (higher BAI scores) significantly preferred general anesthesia for caesarean delivery, while those with lower anxiety levels preferred spinal anesthesia.
cross-section timing: During pre-operative examinations at the anesthesia clinic
